recognize_zh: 骨髓切骨小樑之間出現多團放射狀、針狀排列並呈彩色雙折射的結晶玫瑰花團（箭頭），周圍被纖維化組織與異物巨細胞反應包圍，是草酸鹽結晶沉積 (oxalosis) 的特徵。
features: Multiple rosettes of radially arranged, needle-shaped crystals showing bright birefringence under partially polarized light (arrow)
Crystal aggregates surrounded by a rim of histiocytes and multinucleated foreign-body giant cells
Marked fibrosis replacing the intertrabecular marrow around the crystal deposits
Irregular bone trabeculae with scalloped surfaces suggesting active remodeling; osteoblast and osteoclast detail limited at this power
Residual hematopoietic marrow with fat preserved at the left edge
describe_en: Bone marrow trephine biopsy shows multiple intertrabecular aggregates of radially arranged, needle-like crystals forming rosettes that are strongly birefringent under polarized light. The crystal deposits are surrounded by a foreign-body giant cell reaction within fibrotic stroma that replaces much of the marrow, and residual hematopoietic marrow is limited to the periphery. The adjacent trabeculae are irregular with scalloped surfaces, suggesting remodeling. Findings are consistent with calcium oxalate crystal deposition in bone marrow (oxalosis), as seen in primary hyperoxaluria or secondary hyperoxalosis with renal failure.

ddx.vs: Urate crystals are needle-shaped and strongly negatively birefringent, typically dissolve in aqueous fixation leaving amorphous tophi, and rarely involve marrow, whereas oxalate forms rosettes that persist in processed tissue.
Crystal-storing histiocytosis shows immunoglobulin crystals within histiocyte cytoplasm, which are non-birefringent or weakly birefringent and light-chain restricted.
Calcium phosphate deposits are basophilic, granular and non-birefringent, lacking radial crystal rosettes.
Infectious granulomas show necrosis and organisms on special stains without polarizable crystals.
